system: You are a careful research assistant classifying public feedback. Output JSON only.
prompt:
Decide for each numbered item whether it is RELEVANT to a study of SIPs (systematic investment plans in mutual funds, incl. auto-invest / monthly mutual-fund investing) with three questions:
  (A) Why do people start a SIP, and what do they expect to happen?
  (B) What changes in their behaviour in the months after starting (checking returns, increasing, reducing, skipping, redeeming, switching, sticking with it)?
  (C) What leads investors to pause, reduce or stop a SIP?

RELEVANT = the text describes the writer's own (or other investors') SIP experience, motives, expectations, behaviour or decisions that speak to A, B or C - including payment/mandate/app problems that make a SIP miss or stop.
NOT RELEVANT = generic praise or complaints about the app, stock trading only, SIPs merely named with nothing about motives/expectations/behaviour/decisions, spam or promotion, thanks to a video creator, or bare how-to questions with no personal situation.
The context line (video or forum topic title) is background only; judge the text.

Return a JSON array with one object per item: [{"i": <item number>, "relevant": true|false}]

ITEMS:

[3] (source: valuepickr; context: Lump Sum Investment in Mutual Fund - Suggestions)
To achieve 20% XIRR, your best bet would be Theory 1.
 You would have to do a combination of SIP plus Lumpsum investments for the same.
 One Lumpsum investment strategy would be to track the PE of the index that you want to invest in, identify a PE level that you are comfortable with, and do a Lumpsum investment everytime the index hits that PE.
 Just curious about your fund category selection. Can you talk more about your thought process for that?(2 flexicap, 1 midcap and 2 smallcap)

[5] (source: valuepickr; context: Lump Sum Investment in Mutual Fund - Suggestions)
Big expectation, even with active/passive funds or mid/small cap funds. We may have to take regular and appropriate actions. As it is hard to predict where our market will be next year, we cannot just keep on investing, expecting a linear return. The current bull run may very well continue but if it does not for any global reason or lack of liquidity from SIPs, we may see no movement for a couple of years. With goal-based investing, time also plays an important role.
 Of course, for people who have direct equity experience, managing MF investing will be easy.
